correctness.rationale: All quantifiers are specified: four possibly dependent generators span R^3, all tetrahedra inside the resulting zonotope allowed. After normalizing a largest triple determinant and orienting generator signs, each remaining coordinate lies in [0,1]. Classical zonotope volume is exactly 8S; the explicit signed four-point tetrahedron has exact edge determinant 8(S+m), establishing the bound for all real inputs without experimentation. Equal minors are necessary for global equality and imply an affine image of the regular rhombic dodecahedron. The supplied standalone exact-integer verifier enumerates all C(14,4)=1001 vertex quadruples and independently evaluates their determinants, confirming a sharp max 20, exactly eight specified maxima, and pairwise intersection at most two. Separate affinity of determinant reduces every interior tetrahedron to vertex combinations and upgrades the no-overlap fact to a complete classification. Cube-plus-six-pyramids volume=16; normalized maximum=5/24. The necessary near-equality minor bounds follow algebraically. No finite test is substituted for any infinite assertion.

The published rhombic-dodecahedron illumination record concerns an unrelated functional. All three highly relevant primary PDFs were materially read. Published-record and primary-literature searches found no stronger result explicitly covering the theorem, but possible unlocated historical equivalents remain a genuine priority risk.

value.rationale: The first genuinely non-parallelotope 3D zonotope class (four Minkowski summands) receives a sharp dimensionless maximum-inscribed-tetrahedron lower bound with a unique affine equality body. The parameter-sensitive strengthening relates a geometric occupancy extremum to the four generator minors and yields a quantitative necessary stability condition. The equality locus consists of eight isolated tetrahedra, unlike generic convex-body phenomena with continuous families. This is a motivated, structural geometric extremum rather than a textbook renaming, arbitrary thin slice, or only a computational count; any historical equivalent would alter its originality assessment.
